subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should Gemini project or quota-bucket identity become an OpenClaw provider/auth routing contract, and should this issue stay as the bucket-specific tracker or fold into the broader provider-profile pool design?
rationale: Current main already handles flat key/profile rotation, but bucket identity adds new config/API semantics and decides whether shared quota state lives in core, provider plugins, or an external sidecar.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Profile Routing
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 as the broader design home while preserving this issue's Gemini bucket requirements as acceptance criteria.

options.title: Keep Bucket Tracker Separate
options.body: Keep this issue open as the dedicated Gemini project-bucket contract until maintainers decide the exact metadata and cooldown semantics.

options.title: Externalize As Sidecar Or Plugin
options.body: Keep core to flat key/profile rotation and ask users to publish bucket-aware key management outside core until a missing plugin API is proven.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provider-Profile Routing
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 as the broader design home while preserving this issue's Gemini bucket requirements as acceptance criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main provider/auth rotation and cooldown implementation history points to xingzhou as the closest code-routing candidate for the decision.
